_README: TEMPLATE — copy to master-facts.json and replace everything with YOUR real history.
Every bullet in a generated resume must cite an id from `facts`. A generated
bullet with no source id is a bug (CLAUDE.md hard rule), so this file is the
single source of truth for anything that can appear on a resume.
All content below is placeholder and must not be used in a real application.
Validate with: node validate-facts.js

facts.text: Cut p99 checkout latency 320ms to 90ms by replacing N+1 ORM reads with a batched Postgres query and a Redis read-through cache.
Reduced paging volume 60% across a 12-service estate by adding SLO-based alerting and deleting 40 threshold alerts that never actioned.
Migrated a 400k-line Python 2 monolith to Python 3 incrementally behind feature flags with zero customer-visible downtime.

_README: What you are actually looking for. filter.js builds its whole candidate
profile from this block, so the facts stay the single source.
archetypes and hard_blockers are REQUIRED — filter.js throws without them.
title_exclusions / title_engineering_signals are OPTIONAL and drive the
deterministic pre-filter, which disqualifies a posting on its title alone
with no API call. Roughly half a typical board is Counsel / Recruiter /
Account Executive, and paying a model to notice that is waste.
A title matching any signal is NEVER pre-filtered, whatever else it says:
that is what keeps 'Backend Engineer, Billing/Tax' out of the bin.
Omit both to use filter.js's defaults, which suit a software engineer.
targets.seniority: Mid-level individual contributor. Not management, not new-grad.
hard_blockers: Requires an active US security clearance
Explicitly states it cannot sponsor a visa at any point
Primarily sales, recruiting, manual QA, or IT support rather than software engineering

_README: Answers to ATS screening questions. These are legal attestations to an
